assets.description: Industrial controllers that regulate pumps and chemical dosing
Operator workstations used to monitor and control the treatment process from the control room
Shared operational and office network carrying both control and business traffic
Historian server archiving sensor readings for regulatory reporting
Maintenance engineer laptop connected to controllers during scheduled servicing

vulnerabilities.description: Industrial controllers may lack authentication, allowing unauthorized commands to be issued directly.
Operator workstations share the same network as office computers, expanding the attack surface to the control environment.
The absence of network segmentation between operational technology and office IT allows lateral movement between domains.
The historian server may be reachable from the office network, exposing regulatory data to unauthorized access.
The maintenance laptop may introduce malware into the controller network if it is not scanned or controlled before connection.
Industrial controllers may run outdated or unpatched firmware, leaving known vulnerabilities exploitable.
The historian server may store data without integrity controls, allowing undetected tampering of regulatory records.

threats.description: An external attacker pivots from a compromised office computer through the shared network to issue malicious commands to industrial controllers.
An external attacker disrupts pump and chemical dosing operations by sending unauthorized commands to industrial controllers via the unsegmented network.
A malicious insider uses an operator workstation to alter process control parameters beyond safe limits.
An external attacker compromises an office computer and moves laterally across the shared network to reach control room workstations.
An external attacker accesses the historian server over the shared network and exfiltrates archived sensor readings.
A malicious insider tampers with historical sensor records on the historian server to falsify regulatory compliance reports.
The maintenance engineer accidentally introduces malware from the laptop to the industrial controllers during a scheduled servicing session.
An external attacker pre-compromises the maintenance laptop so that it delivers malware to controllers when physically connected during servicing.
